newsitem.title: USA: World Series with Yankees could boost NYC economy.
newsitem.headline: World Series with Yankees could boost NYC economy.

text.p: The New York City comptroller on Wednesday said that the city's economy could get a $42.4 million shot in the arm if the Yankees baseball team were to play all seven games of the World Series.

The total potential amount of revenue the Bronx Bombers could contribute to the city's economy when division and league championship and World Series games are taken into account could be as much as $69 million, the comptroller said.

But Alan Hevesi lowered the forecast he made last week, when he predicted that the city stood to capture as much as $84 million from increased ticket sales and broadcasting fees, bigger hotel, bar and restaurant bills and indirect spending.

The city now stands to make less because the Yankees beat the Baltimore Orioles in five games. That deprived the city of the economic benefits it would have captured had the last two games of that series been played at Yankee Stadium.

"When we're watching the Yankees' thrilling come-from-behind wins, none of us thinks about jobs. But when Bernie Williams slams a homer and Andy Pettite baffles a batter, it is not just exciting, it makes New York's economy stronger," Hevesi said, in prepared remarks.
The Yankees winning the division championship against the Texas Rangers was worth $10.8 million to the city, he estimated.
And by beating the Rangers and getting into the American League Championship, the team produced another $15.8 million.
The World Series will contribute $21.2 million if only two games are played in Yankee Stadium and $42.4 million if the Series goes the full seven games and four are played here.
